entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Flavius Dioscorus lived during the 6th century AD in the village of Aphrodito, Egypt, and therefore is called by modern scholars Dioscorus of Aphrodito. Although he was an Egyptian, he composed poetry in Greek, the lingua franca of the Eastern Mediterranean since the Hellenistic period. The manuscripts, which contain his corrections and revisions, were discovered on papyrus in 1905, and are now held in museums and libraries around the world. Dioscorus was also occupied in legal work, and legal documents and drafts involving him, his family, Aphroditans, and others were discovered along with his poetry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dioscorus of Aphrodito's poetry and legal work provide insight into the literary and juridical practices of the Eastern Mediterranean during the Byzantine period. His manuscripts offer a unique window into the cultural and intellectual landscape of late antiquity.
